draft.title: Costs and benefits of a decision
card: Every choice gives you something and takes something away. Before deciding, list what each choice gives and what it takes.
something good you gain from a choice, such as money, enjoyment, a new skill or help for other people.
something you give up or use because of a choice. It can be money, time or effort, and it can also be an effect on other people.
Compare the lists for each choice. Costs and benefits can fall on others as well as on you, so include them.
draft.remember: List the benefits and costs of each choice, including money, time and effects on others.

a.q: Sam is deciding whether to spend Saturday mornings training for a swimming club. Which is a cost of this choice?
opts: The time he can no longer spend on other activities
The fitness he gains from regular training
The friends he makes at the club
The fun he has in the pool
a.why: Training uses up Sam's Saturday mornings, so time is a cost. Fitness, friends and fun are things he gains, so they are benefits, even though the club choice might feel like effort.
a.clue: A cost is something given up or used.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Hobart. She thinks about opening on Sundays. It would bring in more sales, but she would work longer hours and her neighbours might hear early deliveries. Which of these is a cost that falls on other people?
opts: Neighbours being disturbed by early deliveries
Priya giving up her own day of rest
Extra money from selling more bread
The cost of paying staff on Sundays
b.why: The neighbours are not part of the bakery's business, and the noise would affect them, so it is a cost to others. Priya's lost rest and staff pay are costs to her and the bakery, and the extra sales are a benefit.
b.clue: Look for the cost that lands on someone outside the bakery.

a.best: The time he can no longer spend on other activities

b.best: Neighbours being disturbed by early deliveries

problems.detail: The why ends with 'even though the club choice might feel like effort', which is confusing. The card lists effort as a cost, but this phrase seems to wave effort away rather than count it as a cost.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer that matches the card. The only issue is a confusing phrase in why (a) about effort, which the card counts as a cost.
